_doc: THE SHARED AI DESIGN (libs:ai): the one source of the chat's look and of its composer, taken from Cloud Code's AI page. Compose reads it through AiDesign (every size here is px on the web and dp/sp in Compose, 1:1); Cloud Code (HTML) reads it through tools/resolve-targets.py, which copies this whole file into targets.gen.json chat.design, and src/cloud/chat/view.js sets each `metrics` entry as the CSS custom property --ai-<key with dashes> on the chat panel, so cloud.scss restates no number. Nothing else in the fleet draws a chat: an app only declares which composer controls it enables and its config bar's first state (Kotlin apps: assets/ai/composer.json, Cloud Code: nav.json::chat.composer).

composer._doc: The composer's bottom config bar, left to right, in THIS order whichever subset an app enables: (+), Task, Agent, Model, Effort, Perms, MCP, (More). `icon` is a class of Cloud Code's icon font (src/res/icons/style.css, proved by its tester); Compose draws the control's glyph itself (AiComposerBar). A selected Task greys Agent and Model: they show the task's mapped ones (ai-tasks.json) and cannot be changed until the task is cleared. The whole bar collapses to ONE compact chip (the active task, else the model) behind a chevron; the state is remembered per app (`collapse`).

layout._doc: The two-row layout of the Compose chat (Cloud SuperIntel; AiComposerBar twoRows). Cloud Code and the other apps keep `controls` above, in its order, untouched. `row` 0 = the input row ((+) attachments dropdown), 1 = toolbar row 1 (Task, Specialist | Agent, Model, Effort, Mode), 2 = toolbar row 2 (Plugins-Skills | KG-Store, KG-Cloud-apps | KG-Repos, KG-Cloud-infra, Plugins-Perf | More); `divider_before` draws a visible bar before that control. An id of `controls` takes its label and icon from there; the others declare theirs. KG-Store opens a full tabbed page (kg_store); KG-Cloud-apps and KG-Cloud-infra are MCP pickers (mcp.buckets); KG-Repos picks the repositories exposed to the model. The single `mcp` control has no place here.

collapse._doc: Chevron toggle at the bar's end. `default` is the first state of an app that never toggled (expanded); the state is kept per app under `pref_key` in the app's own SharedPreferences (Cloud Code: localStorage) so it survives restarts.

plus._doc: The (+) menu: Attach (Files through the system document picker, any type; Image through the photo picker; Camera takes a picture into a temp file, then attaches it; an item is shown only when the app wires it) and New chat. Camera and media access are libs:perms rows, never asked here: a missing one shows the compact Fix in Perms chip.

permission._doc: The Permission Mode's choices. No backend the gateway fronts takes a per-request approval switch today, so a mode is sent as a standing system instruction (via = prompt), exactly as Cloud Code always did; an agent that grows a real switch gets it declared here as `via: param`. `ask` is the default and adds nothing.

modes.label: Auto-edit
modes.instruction: Permission mode: auto-edit. You may create and edit files without asking. Ask before running commands that change anything outside the files (installs, deploys, pushes, deletions).

modes.label: Read-only
modes.instruction: Permission mode: read-only. Do not change anything and do not run tools that write. Read, search and explain only; say what you would change instead of doing it.

modes.label: Plan
modes.instruction: Permission mode: plan. Do not change anything and do not run tools that write. Read what you need, then answer with a numbered plan and wait for approval.

mcp._doc: The MCPs control toggles the MCP servers the gateway lists for the session (GET ai.json::gateway.mcp_path). The gateway has no per-request server switch yet, so the chosen set rides as a standing instruction; `instruction` is its sentence, {servers} the comma-separated names. An empty selection adds nothing. `buckets` sort a server into the three MCP homes (first match wins, in order: exact name, then prefix; the last bucket takes the rest): KG-Cloud-infra (mesh-only, one so far), KG-Cloud-apps (Cloudy user-facing, non-infra), KG-Store (everything else on the public internet, google-workspace and google-personal included). `known` names are listed in their picker even before the gateway lists them (greyed, 'not listed').
mcp.instruction: MCP servers for this session: use only {servers} when you call tools.

agents_extra._doc: Gateway modes ai.json lists that the shared agent descriptor (model-catalogue agents.json) does not: `openrouter` runs any OpenRouter model, the model the request names. Task mappings use it. Cloud Code already lists it as its direct backend, so only Compose adds it.

effort._doc: Reasoning effort levels, sent as OpenRouter's reasoning.effort (low, medium, high, max; verified 2026-10-10 in Cloud Code's nav.json) when picked; `auto` sends nothing and leaves the model's own default. A model that does not reason ignores the field.

more._doc: The More sheet: groups with headers, each with items. kind: usage = tokens and cost the backend REPORTED (per session and per day; the Costs ledger in Cloud Tools; nothing is invented, a backend that reports nothing says so); plugins = the gateway's optimisation plugins that its live /health.plugins lists, each a request-header toggle (`header`, `plugin`); prompt = fills the input with `prompt` (nothing is sent until the user does); export = the open session as Markdown; system = the standing system prompt in force; info = the declared `text`; retry / undo act on the last exchange. An item with a `class` (skill | performance) is shown in the Plugins -> Skills / Plugins: performance picker of a two-row app, and left out of its More sheet; an app without those controls keeps them here.

items.label: Skills and toolsets
items.prompt: List the skills and toolsets you can use right now, one line each.

items.label: Memory
items.prompt: What do you remember about me and my current work? Read your memory first.

items.label: Keyboard shortcuts
items.text: Enter sends on a hardware keyboard; Shift+Enter adds a line. The chevron at the end of the bar collapses it.

items.label: About
items.text: The fleet's one AI chat (libs:ai), Cloud Code's design. Task, agent, model, effort, permission mode and MCP servers are sent with every request; nothing here holds a token.

repos._doc: The Repos picker: which repositories the model may see (an app's list is composer.json::repos). The chosen set rides as a standing instruction, like the MCP sentence; {repos} is the comma-separated names. An empty selection adds nothing.
repos.instruction: Repositories exposed to you for this session: {repos}. Read code from these only.

kg_store._doc: The KG-Store page (a full page with tabs, like the Model Catalogue): public-web sources the model may use. kind: web = the chat's own web-search switch; source = a public source whose choice rides as a standing instruction ({sources}); mcp = an MCP server (its toggle is the MCPs selection). The last tab lists whatever other internet MCPs the gateway lists.
kg_store.instruction: Public sources to use for this session: {sources}.

items.label: Web search
items.detail: public internet, the model's own or OpenRouter search

items.label: Fetch public pages
items.detail: read a URL you give it

items.detail: GitHub releases of the fleet repos
